text: Problem set 7 Problem 1. Is the set of polynomials p1(x) = x3 + 2x, p2(x) = x2 + x + 1, p3(x) = x3 + 5 linear independent or dependent in P3(R)? Justify your answer. Problem 2. Determine for which values of k the following matrix in M3×3(R) is invert- ible, and find the inverse when it exists:  1 k 0 k 1 0 0 1 1   . Problem 3. Let V be an n-dimensional vector space over F . The set V m consists of elements the form (v1, . . . , vm) for vi ∈ V , 1 ≤ i ≤ m. (You can think of V m the same as Mn×m(F ) where each matrix A = (v1, . . . , vm) ∈ Mn×m(F ) is though of as m columns of vectors vi ∈ F n.) An alternating m-linear form (or simply m-form) is a function ω : V m → F satisfying 1. ω is multilinear: If for some 1 ≤ j ≤ n, vj = ax + by where a, b ∈ F x, y ∈ F n, then ω(v1, . . . , ax + by, . . . , vm) = aω(v1, . . . , x, . . . , vm) + bω(v1, . . . , y, . . . , vm). 2. ω alternative: If vi = vj for i ̸= j, then ω(v1, . . . , vm) = 0. The set of all m-forms on V is denoted by ⋀m V ∗. It can be shown that this is a vector space over F under natural addition and scalar multiplication. Note that a 1-form is just a linear function on V and so ⋀1 V ∗ = V ∗. The determinant is an n-form on F n. (i) Show that if ω ∈ ⋀m V ∗ then ω(v1, . . . , 0, . . . , vm) = 0 and if m ≥ 2 then for any λi ∈ F ω(v1, . . . , vj + ∑ i̸=j λivi, . . . , vm) = ω(v1, . . . , vj, . . . , vm). (ii) Show that if {v1, . . . , vm} are linearly dependent, then ω(v1, . . . , vm) = 0. (iii) Show that if m > n = dim V ≥ 1, then for any ω ∈ ⋀m V ∗ and v1, . . . , vm ∈ V , we have ω(v1, . . . , vm) = 0. In other words, ⋀m V ∗ = {0}. Remark 1. We have seen in class that the determinant is the signed n-dimensional volume. Up to scaling, an m-form is computing the signed m-dimensional volume of the parallelepiped spanned by (v1, . . . , vm) projected to some m-dimensional subspace. For example, consider the dual basis (φ1, . . . , φn) of a basis (v1, . . . , vn) of V . Each φi is a 1-form and φi(v) is computing the signed 1-dimensional volume of v projected to vi, i.e. the component of the projection of v to vi. 1 Problem 4.
